enforcement_order: reject transport frame over max_request_bytes before UTF-8 decode or json.loads
pre-scan or bounded parser enforces depth before recursive stdlib decoder can exhaust stack
strict parse rejects duplicate keys, floats, non-finite numbers, and unsafe integers
single iterative structural pass enforces node/member/array/string/reference totals
typed CaseRequestV4 validation enforces field-specific 512-reference caps
deadline is checked across decode, parse, structural validation, and typed validation
basis: V4 is a reference envelope, not a raw dossier-text transport; a 256 KiB default accommodates two 512-reference vectors with digest-form references
1 MiB hard byte cap bounds allocation before parsing; structural caps remain necessary because tiny JSON tokens can create many nodes
depth 32 is well above the current request shape while staying far below the local strict-parser RecursionError observed at depth 3072; depth 2048 still parsed on this host
50,000 nodes, 128 members/object, 1,024 items/array, and 64 KiB/string are conservative hard bounds exercised directly by named samples
1,536 default and 2,048 hard total-reference caps accommodate the two existing 512-item vectors plus scalar closed-contract references without weakening either per-field 512 cap
250 ms default and 1,000 ms hard admission deadlines are parser-abuse circuit breakers with headroom over the local boundary sample; they are not service latency SLOs
